==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|instructour||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{uder|en|la|instructor}}, equivalent to {{af|en|instruct|-or|id2=agent noun}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪnˈstɹʌktɚ/|a=GA}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-instructor.wav|a=Southern England}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-AnotherFriendlyHuman-instructor.wav|a=US}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# One who [[instruct]]s; a [[teacher]].
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=2014-03-14|title=Life without tenure: how I've found fulfilment in US academia|author=Jacqueline Taylor
|text=According to the National Centre for Education Statistics' most recent numbers (2012), 50% of '''instructors''' at degree-granting institutions in the US are part-time. {{...}} Through teaching as an adjunct '''instructor''' while still a graduate student, I've had the luxury of developing my career: testing out teaching strategies, exploring innovative courses, and developing relationships with students – all while working on my dissertation.
|url=https://www.theguardian.com/higher-education-network/blog/2014/mar/14/adjunct-university-united-states-teaching-phd-students-instructor-tenure|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261018134017/https://www.theguardian.com/higher-education-network/blog/2014/mar/14/adjunct-university-united-states-teaching-phd-students-instructor-tenure|archivedate=18 October 2026}}

====Synonyms====
* {{l|en|instructer}} {{q|much less common}}

====Hyponyms====

* {{l|en|instructrix}} {{q|female, dated}}
